name: happiness
quote: I got that job I really wanted!
description: Something happened that is perceived to positively affect an important identity and future experiences.

variations.name: surprise happiness
variations.description: Unexpected love, hope, wonder, or other pleasant experiences can create a sense that the future is something to look forward to.

variations.name: existential happiness
variations.description: A sense that what just happened significantly improves your life story.

commentaries.quote: Happiness may be the opposite of sadness, but the brain chemicals don't last nearly as long. We can't ruminate on happiness to keep it alive like we do for sadness.
Joy is the long-smoldering remnant of happiness.
It's not necessary for anything to actually change to cause happiness. A shift in perception is enough.

Happiness is not something that you can find, acquire, or achieve directly. You have to get the conditions right and then wait. Some of those conditions are within you, such as coherence among the parts and levels of your personality. Other conditions require relationships to things beyond you: Just as plants need sun, water, and good soil to thrive, people need love, work, and a connection to something larger. It is worth striving to get the right relationships between yourself and others, between yourself and your work, and between yourself and something larger than yourself. If you get these relationships right, a sense of purpose and meaning will emerge.

conditions: A perception of the environment has changed favorably.
You predict many more higher valence experiences are coming.
